L5.1.quote: For $f(x)=x+c$ ($c\ge 0$) the original inequalities become \[\sqrt{\frac{x^2 + (y+c)^2}{2}} \ge \frac{x+y+c}{2} \ge \sqrt{x(y+c)} ,\] which are exactly the Quadratic‑Mean–Arithmetic‑Mean inequality and the Arithmetic‑Mean–Geometric‑Mean inequality applied to the two positive numbers $x$ and $y+c$.
L5.1.note: Both inequalities verified for all x,y>0 and every c>=0.

L5.2.quote: Put $x = f(y)$ ... the chain collapses to equality: $\bigl(f(f(y)) + y\bigr)^2 = 4f(y)^2 .$ Taking square roots (all terms are positive) yields f(f(y)) + y = 2f(y)
L5.2.note: Correct derivation; equivalently g(x+g(x))=g(x), giving arithmetic progressions.

L5.3.note: Only g(x) > -x noted; negative differences never excluded, yet V ⊆ {0,c} is asserted from 'at most one positive value'.

L5.4.quote: Suppose $V$ contains two distinct positive numbers $c_1 > c_2 > 0$ ... For large $t$ the inequality is violated – contradiction. ... the set $\{n c_1 - m c_2\}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$ ... the right‑hand side of (9) tends to $0$ while the left‑hand side tends to $+\infty$
L5.4.note: Both rational and irrational ratio cases treated completely via inequality (7).

L5.5.quote: From (11) we immediately obtain $(x-y)^2 > c^2$, hence $|x-y| > c$ ... If $x \in S_0$, then by (12) we must have $|x - (u + n c)| > c$ ... Hence $S_0 = \emptyset$.
L5.5.note: Mixed fixed/non-fixed case excluded rigorously, but the dichotomy f(x)∈{x,x+c} rests on unproved nonnegativity of g.

parsed.notes: Sufficiency is fully verified (both inequalities, all c>=0). Structural identity and the equal-positive-differences argument are complete. Necessity is nearly complete: Lemma 1, (12) and the covering argument kill the mixed case, but negative values of g = f - x are never ruled out, so V ⊆ {0,c} is unjustified.
